name: Passkey availability checks
plain: A page can ask whether this device can use a passkey, without showing a prompt.
meaning: Static checks such as PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() and getClientCapabilities() say whether a built in authenticator, passkey autofill or a phone passkey is possible. Sites use them to decide what to show. The answers also reveal a headless server, virtual machine or container, which often has no authenticator.

access.iframe: Needs a permissions policy in cross origin frames
steps: Browser answers true or false with no prompt
Page picks the sign in screen and may add the answer to a risk score

fields.name: uvpaa
fields.range: true when a built in authenticator with user verification exists

fields.name: conditionalMediation
fields.range: true when passkey autofill is available

fields.name: clientCapabilities
fields.range: named features such as hybridTransport and passkeyPlatformAuthenticator

limits.headline: Can tell whether the device is ready for passkeys
can: Check for a built in passkey device
Notice servers and containers that have no authenticator
limits.reach_label: A few yes or no answers
limits.differs: The answers vary by operating system and settings, so a false value is only a hint that the device may be a server.

story.what_it_is: The page can ask your browser a few quiet yes or no questions about passkeys. It never sees your keys.

marketing.name: PublicKeyCredential
marketing.pitch: Docs list the static checks used to decide whether to offer passkeys.

story.for_you: You never see it. A site uses the answers to decide whether to show a passkey button for you.
story.for_makers: Use the checks to choose what to show, but never to block a person. Treat a false answer as a weak risk hint only, since many laptops without biometrics also answer false.

use_cases.example: A login page shows a passkey button only where a built in authenticator exists.
A bank offers passkey autofill when it is available.
A store hides a passkey prompt on devices that cannot use one.
A product team measures what share of visitors can use passkeys.
A fraud team notes that servers and containers answer false.
A tester sets up a virtual authenticator to make the checks pass.

risks: Weak bot hint can penalize real users
